one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-04. Scheduled: Uber Q3 2026 results, expected Tue 2026-11-03 pre-market (aggregators; not yet confirmed by Uber IR, last year was 11-04, so most likely inside the window). Guide: GB $58.25-60.25B, non-GAAP EPS $0.84-0.88, adj. EBITDA $2.86-2.96B. Uber usually lands at or above the top of the GB range but the stock fell ~5% on the Q2 guide, so the reaction is two-sided. Tesla Q3 (late Oct) will carry Cybercab commentary; the Austin Cybercab fleet grew from 58 to 125 vehicles 9/21-9/25 (Teslarati via Yahoo), so robotaxi headlines are a modest negative skew. Waymo city launches continue. Lyft and DoorDash report around/after the window end. The Delivery Hero acceptance period ends 2026-11-05, one day after the window. Verified insider buying (CEO ~$10M at $70.96, COO ~$5.3M) gives mild support near current levels but is not a timing signal. Net: near-symmetric distribution, median ~$69.9, one-month sigma ~11.5% (35%/3.5 = 10%, bumped for earnings inside the window). Unchanged from round 1 in substance.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (17x on ~$4.80 Oct-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS = $81.6), EV/FCF (15x on ~$10.5B post-SBC FCF, net debt $7.3B, listed stakes ~$8B = $79.1) and EV/adj. EBITDA (10.0x on ~$15.9B NTM, = $79.9); weights 40/35/25 give ~$80.

bear.story: Not a 12-month volume loss but a terminal-value de-rating: Waymo scales toward 700k-1M weekly rides with its own app in more markets and signals traction ahead of its Jan-2028 Austin/Atlanta app; Tesla expands Cybercab beyond Austin (fleet already ~125); market extrapolates aggregator disintermediation after 2028. Add a growth wobble (Brazil courier supply, US promo intensity) pushing GB growth to mid-teens and DH leverage/antitrust friction. Multiple compresses to ~11-12x on ~$4.5 EPS.

base.story: GB growth high-teens, EPS +20-25%, FCF ~$12B+. Industry data keep showing AV at low single-digit US share and Uber holding share in AV cities; Waymo stays on Uber through the horizon. No re-rating: ~16-16.5x NTM EPS and ~10x EBITDA, so return comes from EPS compounding plus buybacks.

bull.story: AV fears ease as Uber's AV partner count and city launches show aggregator value and Tesla scaling stalls; CA SB 623 insurance savings lift 2027 US margins; DH closes 2H27 accretive. P/E moves to the peer median ~19.5-20x on ~$5.1 EPS. I cap the bull below round 1's $106 because EBITDA comps do not support a further re-rating (UBER already above the NTM median).

comps_summary.peer_range: Reconciled NTM basis (0.25*FY26 + 0.75*FY27 consensus, prices/EV at 2026-10-05) for 10 peers: P/E 12.8x (EXPE) to 47.7x (DASH), median 19.6x; core-7 (DASH, LYFT, GRAB, CART, ABNB, BKNG, EXPE) 18.0x. EV/EBITDA 6.3x (TCOM) to 19.0x (MELI), median 9.4x; core-7 8.5x. Dropped vs round 1: ETERNAL (early-profit outlier), DHER (pinned to Uber's offer), Meituan (loss-making). Round-1 figures were trailing GAAP / mixed-basis aggregator data.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17.0x P/E is ~13% below the all-peer median and ~6% below the core-7 median (UBER now 16.6x). 10.0x EV/adj. EBITDA is ~6% above the 9.4x median and below UBER's current 11.1x. Blended, roughly at the peer midpoint.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: P/E discount: the Waymo own-app launch in Austin/Atlanta (Jan-2028, alongside Uber, contract to at least May 2028) and Tesla Cybercab growth are post-horizon terminal risks that will not be resolved within 12 months, so a small discount persists. EBITDA premium: small and inside the range, justified by structurally faster EBITDA growth (+33% YoY in Q2, ~20%+ forward consensus) than the low-multiple peers (LYFT, CART, EXPE, TCOM) and by Uber's scale/multi-product margins; trimmed for SBC. No sell-side outperformance calls used. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] Sourcing note: the 19.6x / 18.0x P/E and 9.4x / 8.5x EV/EBITDA medians (and UBER 16.6x / 11.1x) came from aggregator multiples (round-1 MarketScreener GAAP-mixed P/E; stockanalysis EV). Rebuilt from each company's Q2 2026 release (EV) and S&P Global adjusted NTM consensus EPS, the all-peer medians are 16.6x P/E (core-7 13.3x) and 9.2x EV/EBITDA (core-7 7.9x); UBER is 16.7x and 11.3x. The per-peer values in this file are left as the agent's round-2 read; supervisor.json comps_review carries the verified table.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$52 the stock would trade near 11x my Oct-2027 NTM EPS and ~10x post-SBC FCF, below every core peer except EXPE/BKNG on P/E, i.e. the market pricing real share loss, not sentiment. That most likely means something fundamental: Uber guiding GB growth well below mid-teens, AV operators (Waymo own app, Tesla) showing measurable off-platform share gains in major US metros before 2028, AV partners pulling cars off Uber earlier than the contract term, or the Delivery Hero deal re-cut at a much higher cost/leverage. A -25% move from $70 without such news is uncommon at 35% vol.

reasoning: Round 2. Supervisor fact-checks changed three things for me. (1) Waymo framing: Waymo launches its own app in Austin/Atlanta in Jan-2028 alongside Uber, with cars on Uber at least through May 2028 and Uber free to add other AVs (TheNextWeb citing an Uber spokesperson; CNBC headline). Both dates fall after the horizon, so I moved this from a 12-month volume risk to a terminal-value/multiple risk in the bear case. (2) Comps: my round-1 medians (22.1x P/E, 31.5x EV/EBITDA) were trailing/mixed-basis aggregator data. On the reconciled NTM basis the median is 19.6x P/E and 9.4x EV/EBITDA, with UBER at 16.6x and 11.1x. My 10.5x EBITDA multiple was above the median, not at the low end; I cut it to 10.0x (a small, argued growth premium) and capped the bull case. (3) Balance sheet: $12.7B debt = $2.0B short-term + $10.7B long-term; using 8-K cash of $5.4B gives $7.3B net debt, not stockanalysis' $4.74B, which cost ~$1.3/share in the FCF and EBITDA legs. Industry follow-up: the Tesla Cybercab fleet grew to ~125 by 9/25 (Teslarati via Yahoo), which corrects my round-1 'fell back to ~8' framing; it is still tiny against Uber's ~3.9B quarterly trips. Waymo's 1M weekly-ride target looks likely to be missed (FutureSearch median ~713k for Q4; snippet only, weak). Lyft/DoorDash read-through on demand remains healthy (Lyft partner rides ~30% of NA rides in Q2). MarketScreener consensus NTM EPS at Oct-27 is ~$5.48; I keep $4.80, a ~12% haircut for AV, Brazil and DH costs. I keep 17x P/E (below the core median) and disagree mildly with the supervisor's 9.5x EBITDA, preferring 10.0x for growth. Fair value falls $82 -> $80. Scenarios $52/78/100 at 25/50/25 (mean $77). Ladder = average of a lognormal (median $74.5, 38% vol, down from $77) and the scenario mixture; median ~$76, P(>=$70) 0.59 (from 0.62), lowering the upper tail most. 1-month ladder essentially unchanged: earnings inside the window, symmetric around ~$69.9 with ~11.5% sigma. Dropped eciks.org per supervisor. No option data or priors consulted. Research limited to ~9 follow-up queries.
